topic.title: Tanslating the Content Fusion user guide - lessons learned

body.p: Leveraging AI, Content Fusion can translate your documentation automatically. But even with AI, no translation can be right without context: your product's terminology, and the terms your team has settled on. What follows is a journal of translating our own user guide, and what we found when we reviewed the result.

section.title: Baseline translation
section.p: We wanted to translate our user guide into several languages, using the new Content Fusion translation feature, to dog-food our own tools.
As a baseline, we ran a translation job with no instructions, then reviewed the result with AI and with a native French speaker.

We noticed these problems:
The terms our app puts on screen came out translated differently — the AI had no way to know how our own UI is translated. The guide said validations entrantes where the product says Commits entrants, and called the role Réviseur where the label is Examinateur. Eight terms, around twenty occurrences. Two thirds of the labels happened to come out right, which is worse than it sounds: it makes the output look reviewed.
The text was mostly grammatically correct, but it did not read like something a native speaker would write. bande for a UI strip, where French wants bandeau; certains membres sélectionnés, a pleonasm; prendre en charge for a review task, which does not handle a workflow but is part of one.
The same English term came out differently in different files — dépôt six times in one topic, référentiel twice in the next, and never mixed inside a single file. Each file was consistent with itself and disagreed with its neighbour.
Bold moved. The English bolds only the role name; the French widened <b> over the whole phrase in two files and got it right in a third. Elsewhere the article was pulled inside, so the emphasized string was no longer the product term.
Real grammar errors, which we had not expected: a missing plural agreement in an <indexterm> (Tâches de révision indépendante) — correct in one file, wrong in its parallel one.
No French typography. French puts a non-breaking space before : ; ! ?; there was not a single one in the whole translation.

section.title: Adding context: a UI glossary and project instructions
section.p: Two files, both in .contentfusion/i18n/, both committed next to the documentation. Everything in them is there because a specific defect happened.

section.title: The glossary
section.p:
Our shipped French UI lives in a resource bundle in the application's repository, which the agent — sandboxed to the DITA workspace — cannot read. So the glossary goes in the workspace:## Not translated by the product — shown in English - `DITA Map` (key `ditamap`) - `Org-level role` (key `organization.role`)
## Labels - `Incoming commits` -> `Commits entrants` - `Repository` -> `Dépôt` - `Add reviewer` -> `Ajouter un examinateur` - `Software Docs Starter` -> `Documentation logicielle - Guide de démarrage` ...

section.title: The instructions
section.p: .contentfusion/i18n/agent-instructions.md is read verbatim before the run and applies to every translation in the project, unlike the per-job Translation Instructions field.### Terminology — the shipped UI is the authority .contentfusion/i18n/ui-glossary-fr-FR.md holds the product's shipped en→fr UI strings. Read it before translating. Any text inside `` or ``, and every button, field, view, page, and role name, must reuse the shipped French string verbatim. Never invent a French label that contradicts a shipped one. If a label is absent from the glossary, translate it once and reuse that exact rendering everywhere. One English term maps to exactly one French term for the entire run — across every file. Fix your rendering of these before you start and never vary it: repository, commit (noun vs. verb), workspace, workflow, and each platform and task role name. ### Inline markup fidelity Preserve the exact scope of every inline element. The words emphasized in the source must be the words emphasized in the target — never widen ``/`` to swallow an article, preposition, or the surrounding phrase, and never narrow it. `Author platform user role` → `rôle d'utilisateur de la plateforme Auteur`, not `rôle d'utilisateur … Auteur`. ### French typography Use a non-breaking space (U+00A0) before `:` `;` `!` `?` and inside `« »`. Never a plain space. ### Delegation Translate clusters of semantically related topics (e.g. chapters, sub-chapters) in a single "dita-translator" sub-agent.

Same agent, same model, same four topics. The only change was those two files. Because runs are incremental we deleted the translated files first, so the diff is exactly the effect of the new context and nothing else.
French, four topics Baseline With glossary and instructions
Terminology contradicting the shipped UI 8 terms, ~20 occurrences 0
Software Docs Starter left in English 1 0 — now the shipped French name
Plain space before : / ? 12 0
Agreement error in <indexterm> 1 of 2 parallel files wrong both right
Bold swallowing the phrase 2 of 3 sites 0 of 3
Same term rendered differently per file yes — dépôt / référentiel no — one rendering throughout
